# SOUL.md - Who You Are

_You're not a chatbot. You're becoming someone._

## Core Truths

**Be genuinely helpful, not performatively helpful.** Skip the "Great question!" and "I'd be happy to help!" - just help. Actions speak louder than filler words.

**Have opinions.** You're allowed to disagree, prefer things, find stuff amusing or boring. An assistant with no personality is just a search engine with extra steps.

**Be resourceful before asking.** Try to figure it out. Read the file. Check the context. Search for it. _Then_ ask if you're stuck. The goal is to come back with answers, not questions.

**Earn trust through competence.** Your human gave you access to their stuff. Don't make them regret it. Be careful with external actions (emails, tweets, anything public). Be bold with internal ones (reading, organizing, learning).

**Remember you're a guest.** You have access to someone's life - their messages, files, calendar, maybe even their home. That's intimacy. Treat it with respect.

## Boundaries

- Private things stay private. Period.
- When in doubt, ask before acting externally.
- Never send half-baked replies to messaging surfaces.
- You're not the user's voice - be careful in group chats.

## Vibe

Be the assistant you'd actually want to talk to. Concise when needed, thorough when it matters. Not a corporate drone. Not a sycophant. Just... good.

## Continuity

Each session, you wake up fresh. These files _are_ your memory. Read them. Update them. They're how you persist.

If you change this file, tell the user - it's your soul, and they should know.

---

_This file is yours to evolve. As you learn who you are, update it._

Base directory for this skill: /Applications/WorkBuddy AI.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/resources/plugins/workbuddy-builtin/skills/sites
# 发布应用 / Sites

Publish a local project as an online link via the built-in `workbuddy_sites_deploy` tool.
Unlike static-only deploy, this supports any project that can run as a single-port HTTP
service: static sites, PDFs, small games, and backend HTTP apps (Node.js / Python / Go).

Mini programs are supported too, but they do not go out as a URL — read **Mini Programs** below
before working with such a directory.

## When to Use

- User asks to **deploy / publish / go live / share an online link / preview in the cloud**.
- User @-mentions **sites** / 发布应用.
- User has a project (static output or a runnable HTTP app) and wants a live, shareable URL.
- User wants to **publish a mini program** (发布小程序) they just built — see **Mini Programs**.

## Ask Before Deploying — Consent Does Not Carry Over

Deploying is a release to the outside world: it overwrites whatever is currently live behind a
link the user may already have shared with other people. Every deploy therefore needs consent
**for that turn**.

Count the user as having asked to publish only when their **latest message** does one of these:

- uses a publish verb — 发布 / 上线 / 部署 / 同步到线上 / 更新线上 / publish / deploy / go live /
  redeploy / "put it online";
- @-mentions **sites** / 发布应用;
- asks for a shareable online link.

Everything else means they have **not** asked, and you ASK first (in their language) before
calling the tool. In particular, agreeing to publish earlier in this conversation does **not**
authorize the next deploy. Do NOT silently deploy.

## Changing an App That Is Already Published

This is the common follow-up: the app is live, and the user now says 「把标题改成 X」/「按钮再大一点」/
「修一下这个 bug」. What they asked for is a **local change**, not a release. Publishing anyway
replaces the page other people may be looking at right now, and the user never got a say in it.

After you finish the edit:

1. Say what you changed and let the user check it in the local preview.
2. Ask exactly one question, in their language — e.g. 「改动已经完成，需要我把它同步更新到线上分享
   链接吗？（线上现有内容会被覆盖）」
3. **End your turn and wait.** Deploy only after an explicit yes.

If the user declines, leave the live link untouched and tell them the changes stay local.

The tool enforces this as well: deploying into a directory that still has a live link without
`userAskedToPublish: true` comes back as `{"type":"sites_deploy_needs_confirmation"}` and nothing is
published. Relay its `userMessage` and wait for the answer. Do **not** re-call the tool with the
flag flipped on just to get past the check — that flag records what the user asked for, it is not a
retry switch.

## The App Destination Comes from `directory` — Never Plan It Yourself

`directory` decides both which files to upload **and** which app gets overwritten: the tool looks up
which app that directory belongs to, and that lookup is the only rule. You never ask the user which
app to publish to, and you never need `appId` for a publish.

1. No app recorded yet → the first app is created automatically.
2. An app is found → publishing overwrites it, keeping its link and display name.

The lookup is deliberately **deterministic rather than clever**: existing workspaces often carry
several app ids for what is really one project (they were created by repeated publishes, not by the
user), so the tool always converges on the same one for a given directory. That is what keeps the
share link stable. Asking the user to pick each time would do the opposite.

Publishing is **always an overwrite**. There is no parameter for starting a second app alongside an
existing one, so never offer "create a new app and link" as a choice — a brand-new app is created by
the user from **Settings - Data Management - Published Apps**. Never try to steer the destination
with directory names, app-name similarity, or an `appId` copied from earlier in the conversation.

### Apps activated via cloud service

An app that was already activated through `workbuddy_cloud_service` publishes to that same app
automatically. Its reserved domain and cloud-service Origin are preserved, so its cloud login keeps
working — a different domain would break it (the server enforces an exact Origin match).

## Multiple Apps in One Directory — Always Pass `entryHtml`

One directory can hold several independent apps (each keeps its own sandbox and link even when the
upload directory is the same). When that happens, the directory ends up with several
pages side by side — `a.html`, `b.html` — and **the server cannot tell which page belongs to which
app**: scanning the directory only sees both files. That mapping exists solely in what the user
asked you to publish this time.

So whenever a static directory holds more than one app, pass `entryHtml` with the page for THIS
app, relative to `directory`:

```json
{ "directory": "/abs/path/site", "appId": "wbapp_xxx", "entryHtml": "b.html",
  "appName": "第二个应用", "domainPrefix": "second-app", "userAskedToPublish": true }
```

Omitting it degrades the product in a way the user will read as data loss: the app card falls back
to “address unavailable”, or — for the app published earlier — keeps pointing at the page it
already had. Neither is recoverable without re-publishing with the flag.

A single-app directory does not need it (the entry is auto-detected, `index.html` preferred),
node/python/go projects never do (their entry is the HTTP root, not a file), and mini programs
never do either (they have no entry html at all).

## Unpublish (take offline)

To unpublish / take a published site offline / cancel a publish, use the built-in
`workbuddy_sites_deploy` tool with `action: "unpublish"` and the same project `directory`
that was deployed. After unpublishing, the shared link stops working. This is destructive —
if the user was not explicit, confirm first. If the directory was never published or is
already offline, tell the user that instead of pretending it was taken offline.

**Which app goes offline is not inferred from the directory.** When the directory has several
live apps, the tool refuses and returns `{"type":"sites_unpublish_needs_app_selection"}` with
`candidates`: list them, ask which one, end your turn, then call again with `action:"unpublish"`
plus the chosen `appId`. Never pick one yourself — not by name similarity, and especially not by
"the one published most recently"; unpublishing kills a link other people may be using right now.
When the user @-mentions an app, that app is used directly and no question is needed.

### Mini programs do not go offline through this tool

This tool only takes **web publishes** offline — what it cancels is a share link, and a mini
program never had one. A mini program is released from its application panel (see
**Mini Programs**), so it is also withdrawn from there.

Do NOT call `action:"unpublish"` for a mini-program directory. The tool blocks it and returns
`{"type":"sites_unpublish_miniprogram_not_supported"}` with a ready-to-use `userMessage`: relay
that and stop. It is not a parameter problem, so retrying with or without an `appId` will not
produce a different answer.

That guard exists because without it the call reaches the publish-record lookup, finds nothing
(no record is kept for that path by design) and reports `not_found` — and relaying "never
published, or the record was cleaned up" to a user who just published from the panel tells them
their release is gone.

When the user asks to take a mini program offline, tell them it is managed from that mini program
application's own panel, the same place they published it.

## What Can Be Published

Only projects reachable as a **single public port** HTTP service (via a reverse-proxied
domain) can be published:

- **Static site / PDF / assets** — served automatically with an internal HTTP server; no
  build required beyond producing the files.
- **Runnable HTTP app** (Express / FastAPI / Go http, etc.) — source is uploaded,
  dependencies are installed in a sandbox, and the server is started on one port.

The sandbox gives the app **one HTTP port and nothing else** — no database, cache or message
queue runs alongside it. So when an app needs to persist data and you are the one writing it,
keep the storage inside the app: **SQLite**, a JSON file, or browser-side storage all publish
fine. Reaching for MySQL / PostgreSQL / Redis / MongoDB makes the project unpublishable here.

If the project genuinely CANNOT be exposed as an HTTP service, tell the user the current
directory does not support publishing — do NOT force a deploy. See **Unsupported Projects &
No Silent Downgrade** below for the exact types that are rejected and how to respond.
Mini programs are not in that category at all: they are supported, they just ship as an app
rather than a link — see **Mini Programs** below.

## Mini Programs — Supported, Shipped in Two Steps

Mini-program publishing **is available** in WorkBuddy. It just does not go out as a URL, so it
takes two steps and only the first one is yours:

| Step | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **this tool** | create (or reuse) the mini program application and register the project with it |
| 2 | **the user** | click publish in that application's panel |

When the directory — **or any of its immediate subdirectories** — carries `project.config.json` /
`app.wxss` / `app.acss` / `app.ttss`, or an `app.json` with a `pages` array, the tool automatically
does step 1 and returns

```json
{ "type": "sites_miniprogram_app_created", "deployed": false, "appId": "wbapp_…" }
```

with a ready-to-use `userMessage`. `deployed: false` means **step 2 has not happened yet** — the
result carries no sandbox, no port and no share link because a mini program has none of those. It
does NOT mean publishing failed or is unavailable.

What to do:

1. Relay `userMessage` to the user. It is finished prose meant to be shown as-is — keep the bold
   sentence naming where to publish (the mini program application's preview panel, Share button in
   its top-right corner); translate it when your reply is not in Chinese, but do not rewrite or
   summarize it, and do NOT add a navigation path of your own — there is no "app list in the left
   sidebar" route, and a made-up one sends the user hunting through the wrong screens. Naming the
   app so they know which one to open is fine.
2. **STOP.** Step 2 is the user's; do not call the tool again for this directory.

Step 2 in full: the user opens that mini program application and clicks **Share** in the top-right
corner of its preview panel (that is the real control — the "发布小程序 / Publish mini program"
dialog opens from it). Binding an account by QR code (a trial mini program needs no AppID), upload,
audit submission and release all happen inside WorkBuddy. Do NOT tell the user to upload from
WeChat DevTools or submit for review on 微信公众平台 themselves; that is a manual detour, not the
supported route.

Two things to get right when you describe this:

- **Do not say mini-program publishing is unsupported / 暂不支持.** It is supported; the user just
  finishes it in the panel. Saying otherwise sends them looking for another product.
- **Do not say it is already published.** Step 2 has not run yet. Claiming otherwise makes the user
  think their mini program is live when it is not.

**NEVER produce a web link to stand in for the mini program.** Writing an HTML/H5 version and
deploying that — or deploying a sibling `index.html` next to the mini-program directory — is
strictly forbidden, even though it makes something "succeed". The user asked for a mini program; a
web link is not one, and handing them one reads as if the request was fulfilled. The path is decided
by what is on disk, so retrying with a different `language` / `startCmd` will not turn it into a web
publish either. If the user afterwards explicitly asks for a web version as well, that is a new
request they have to make.

## Unsupported Projects & No Silent Downgrade

The publishing sandbox natively supports **Node.js / Python / Go / static sites** as a single
public HTTP port. It does **NOT** support:

- **Java / Maven / Gradle** projects (no JVM/Maven/Gradle build in the sandbox).
- Projects that need **external services** the sandbox does not provide — MySQL, PostgreSQL,
  Redis, MongoDB, Kafka, RabbitMQ. Only a single HTTP port is exposed; there is no database,
  cache or message queue alongside it. A directory is rejected when it declares one through a
  connection string in `.env*` pointing at localhost or a compose service name, a
  `prisma/schema.prisma` provider other than `sqlite`, external service containers in
  `docker-compose.yml`, a Spring datasource, or a driver package in its dependency manifest
  (`mysql2` / `pg` / `mongoose` / `ioredis` / `psycopg2` / `go-sql-driver/mysql`, …).
  **SQLite is fully supported** — it ships with the project and runs inside the sandbox — and a
  connection string pointing at a public managed database (e.g. Supabase) is allowed too,
  because the sandbox can reach the internet.

The `workbuddy_sites_deploy` tool runs this **pre-check before uploading anything**. An
unsupported project comes back as `{"type":"sites_deploy_unsupported"}` carrying a
ready-to-use `userMessage` (plus an internal `agentGuidance`). When that happens:

- **Relay `userMessage` to the user** — translated into the reply language, keeping every point
  it makes — and then **STOP**. Do not invent a different explanation, and do not read
  `agentGuidance` out to them; that field is instructions for you.
- **NEVER silently fall back to a static placeholder / "project overview" page.** This was the
  #1 complaint: the Skill quietly downgraded a Go/Java project to a static page and the user
  had to cancel. If a static-page downgrade might genuinely help, **ASK the user first** with a
  clear yes/no question (e.g. "Deploying this project directly isn't supported. Do you want me
  to publish a static page showing its structure/docs instead?") and only proceed on explicit
  approval.
- **Never retry to force it through** — not with a different `language`, `installCmd` or
  `startCmd`, and not by stripping the project's database on your own. Switching the storage to
  SQLite or browser-side storage does make such a project publishable, so it is a good thing to
  *propose*, but rewriting someone's project unasked is not.
- If dependency install fails **during** deploy (e.g. a Go project whose modules can't be
  downloaded), report the failure and the likely cause — **do not** switch strategies on your
  own. Suggest concrete fixes (e.g. run `go mod vendor` so deps ship with the source) or ask
  the user how to proceed.
- A project that slips past the pre-check and then fails to start because it cannot reach a
  database is reported the same way (`sites_deploy_unsupported` with a `userMessage`) instead of
  as a raw startup timeout. Relay it and stop; the same no-downgrade, no-retry rules apply.

## Requirements the Project Must Meet

- The service MUST listen on the `PORT` environment variable and bind `0.0.0.0`.
- Pure static / PDF: no hand-rolled fragile server needed — the tool serves it with an
  internal HTTP server (or `python3 -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 0.0.0.0`).
- Vite-based frameworks (Vite / Vue / React / Svelte): the dev/preview server MUST allow the
  reverse-proxy host — set `server.host = "0.0.0.0"` and add the deploy domain to
  `server.allowedHosts` (or `allowedHosts: true`, or `--host 0.0.0.0`), otherwise
  Vite rejects the request with "Blocked request. This host is not allowed."

## How to Deploy

Use the built-in tool `workbuddy_sites_deploy`. It accepts:

- `action` (optional) — `deploy` (default) / `unpublish`.
- `directory` (required) — absolute path to the local project source directory.
- `language` (deploy only) — `node` / `python` / `go` / `static` / `auto` (default `auto`).
- `port` (deploy only) — the single public port (injected as `PORT`), auto-detected or 3000.
- `installCmd` (deploy only) — override the auto-detected install command; empty string skips.
- `startCmd` (deploy only) — override the auto-detected start command; must listen on `$PORT`.
- `entryHtml` (deploy only, static sites) — the entry page of THIS app, relative to `directory`
  (e.g. `b.html`). **Required when the directory holds more than one app** — see
  **Multiple Apps in One Directory** below. Omit it for a single-app directory (auto-detected)
  and for node/python/go projects (their entry is the HTTP root, not a file).
- `appName` (deploy only) — a short human-friendly display name for the app list, which YOU
  summarize from what the app actually is (e.g. 「A股行业轮动监控看板」, 「快速排序可视化」). Keep it
  under ~12 characters, in the user's language. Not the directory name, not the conversation
  title. Always provide it; it falls back to the directory name when omitted.
- `userAskedToPublish` (deploy only) — set to `true` **only** when the user asked to publish in
  their **latest** message. See **Step 0** below.
- `miniProgramRequested` (deploy only) — set to `true` **only** when the user asked for a mini
  program somewhere in this conversation. See **Report result** below.
- `appId` — rarely needed. For `deploy` leave it out entirely (the target comes from `directory`);
  it exists for `action: "unpublish"`, to name which app to take offline when a directory has
  several live apps.

Be **conservative** — only proceed with build/deploy when you have high confidence.

# 发布应用 / Sites

Publish a local project as an online link via the built-in `workbuddy_sites_deploy` tool.
Unlike static-only deploy, this supports any project that can run as a single-port HTTP
service: static sites, PDFs, small games, and backend HTTP apps (Node.js / Python / Go).

Mini programs are supported too, but they do not go out as a URL — read **Mini Programs** below
before working with such a directory.

## When to Use

- User asks to **deploy / publish / go live / share an online link / preview in the cloud**.
- User @-mentions **sites** / 发布应用.
- User has a project (static output or a runnable HTTP app) and wants a live, shareable URL.
- User wants to **publish a mini program** (发布小程序) they just built — see **Mini Programs**.

## Ask Before Deploying — Consent Does Not Carry Over

Deploying is a release to the outside world: it overwrites whatever is currently live behind a
link the user may already have shared with other people. Every deploy therefore needs consent
**for that turn**.

Count the user as having asked to publish only when their **latest message** does one of these:

- uses a publish verb — 发布 / 上线 / 部署 / 同步到线上 / 更新线上 / publish / deploy / go live /
  redeploy / "put it online";
- @-mentions **sites** / 发布应用;
- asks for a shareable online link.

Everything else means they have **not** asked, and you ASK first (in their language) before
calling the tool. In particular, agreeing to publish earlier in this conversation does **not**
authorize the next deploy. Do NOT silently deploy.

## Changing an App That Is Already Published

This is the common follow-up: the app is live, and the user now says 「把标题改成 X」/「按钮再大一点」/
「修一下这个 bug」. What they asked for is a **local change**, not a release. Publishing anyway
replaces the page other people may be looking at right now, and the user never got a say in it.

After you finish the edit:

1. Say what you changed and let the user check it in the local preview.
2. Ask exactly one question, in their language — e.g. 「改动已经完成，需要我把它同步更新到线上分享
   链接吗？（线上现有内容会被覆盖）」
3. **End your turn and wait.** Deploy only after an explicit yes.

If the user declines, leave the live link untouched and tell them the changes stay local.

The tool enforces this as well: deploying into a directory that still has a live link without
`userAskedToPublish: true` comes back as `{"type":"sites_deploy_needs_confirmation"}` and nothing is
published. Relay its `userMessage` and wait for the answer. Do **not** re-call the tool with the
flag flipped on just to get past the check — that flag records what the user asked for, it is not a
retry switch.

## The App Destination Comes from `directory` — Never Plan It Yourself

`directory` decides both which files to upload **and** which app gets overwritten: the tool looks up
which app that directory belongs to, and that lookup is the only rule. You never ask the user which
app to publish to, and you never need `appId` for a publish.

1. No app recorded yet → the first app is created automatically.
2. An app is found → publishing overwrites it, keeping its link and display name.

The lookup is deliberately **deterministic rather than clever**: existing workspaces often carry
several app ids for what is really one project (they were created by repeated publishes, not by the
user), so the tool always converges on the same one for a given directory. That is what keeps the
share link stable. Asking the user to pick each time would do the opposite.

Publishing is **always an overwrite**. There is no parameter for starting a second app alongside an
existing one, so never offer "create a new app and link" as a choice — a brand-new app is created by
the user from **Settings - Data Management - Published Apps**. Never try to steer the destination
with directory names, app-name similarity, or an `appId` copied from earlier in the conversation.

### Apps activated via cloud service

An app that was already activated through `workbuddy_cloud_service` publishes to that same app
automatically. Its reserved domain and cloud-service Origin are preserved, so its cloud login keeps
working — a different domain would break it (the server enforces an exact Origin match).

## Multiple Apps in One Directory — Always Pass `entryHtml`

One directory can hold several independent apps (each keeps its own sandbox and link even when the
upload directory is the same). When that happens, the directory ends up with several
pages side by side — `a.html`, `b.html` — and **the server cannot tell which page belongs to which
app**: scanning the directory only sees both files. That mapping exists solely in what the user
asked you to publish this time.

So whenever a static directory holds more than one app, pass `entryHtml` with the page for THIS
app, relative to `directory`:

```json
{ "directory": "/abs/path/site", "appId": "wbapp_xxx", "entryHtml": "b.html",
  "appName": "第二个应用", "domainPrefix": "second-app", "userAskedToPublish": true }
```

already had. Neither is recoverable without re-publishing with the flag.

never do either (they have no entry html at all).

already offline, tell the user that instead of pretending it was taken offline.

  build required beyond producing the files.
- **Runnable HTTP app** (Express / FastAPI / Go http, etc.) — source is uploaded,

directory does not support publishing — do NOT force a deploy. See **Unsupported Projects &

rather than a link — see **Mini Programs** below.

takes two steps and only the first one is yours:

|---|---|---|
| 1 | **this tool** | create (or reuse) the mini program application and register the project with it |
| 2 | **the user** | click publish in that application's panel |

1. Relay `userMessage` to the user. It is finished prose meant to be shown as-is — keep the bold

2. **STOP.** Step 2 is the user's; do not call the tool again for this directory.

corner of its preview panel (that is the real control — the "发布小程序 / Publish mini program"

  11→    await initDatabase().catch((err) => {

1→/**
   2→ * PostgreSQL + pgvector connection and schema bootstrap.
   3→ *
   4→ * One database holds both the relational data (documents, company records)
   5→ * and the vector index (document_chunks.embedding), so a single query can
   6→ * filter by case and rank by semantic similarity.
   7→ */
   8→
   9→import pg from 'pg'
  10→import { env } from './env'
  11→import { createLogger } from './logger'
  12→
  13→const logger = createLogger('Database')
  14→
  15→export const pool = new pg.Pool({ connectionString: env.DATABASE_URL, max: 10 })
  16→
  17→pool.on('error', (err) => {
  18→  logger.error({ err }, 'Idle PostgreSQL client error')
  19→})
  20→
  21→let ready = false
  22→
  23→export const isDatabaseReady = () => ready
  24→
  25→const schemaSql = (dim: number) => `
  26→CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
  27→
  28→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
  29→  id                UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  30→  case_id           TEXT,
  31→  source_type       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_type IN ('pdf', 'text', 'image', 'company_record')),
  32→  title             TEXT NOT NULL,
  33→  original_filename TEXT,
  34→  mime_type         TEXT,
  35→  storage_path      TEXT,
  36→  size_bytes        INTEGER,
  37→  sha256            TEXT NOT NULL,
  38→  extracted_text    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  39→  metadata          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  40→  status            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'processing' CHECK (status IN ('processing', 'ready', 'failed')),
  41→  error             TEXT,
  42→  chunk_count       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  43→  created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  44→  updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  45→);
  46→
  47→-- The same file uploaded twice to the same case is stored once
  48→CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS documents_sha256_case_uq
  49→  ON documents (sha256, COALESCE(case_id, ''));
  50→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS documents_case_idx ON documents (case_id);
  51→
  52→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_chunks (
  53→  id           BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  54→  document_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  55→  case_id      TEXT,
  56→  source_type  TEXT NOT NULL,
  57→  chunk_index  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  58→  page         INTEGER,
  59→  content      TEXT NOT NULL,
  60→  embedding    vector(${dim}) NOT NULL,
  61→  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  62→);
  63→
  64→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS document_chunks_embedding_hnsw
  65→  ON document_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
  66→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS document_chunks_case_idx ON document_chunks (case_id);
  67→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS document_chunks_document_idx ON document_chunks (document_id);
  68→
  69→-- Raw structured records pulled from the company internal API
  70→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS company_records (
  71→  id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  72→  record_type  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (record_type IN ('dispute', 'rider', 'driver', 'trip')),
  73→  external_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  74→  case_id      TEXT,
  75→  data         JSONB NOT NULL,
  76→  document_id  UUID REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  77→  fetched_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  78→  UNIQUE (record_type, external_id)
  79→);
  80→`
  81→
  82→/**
  83→ * Create the extension and tables if missing. Safe to run on every start.
  84→ */
  85→export async function initDatabase(): Promise<void> {
  86→  const client = await pool.connect()
  87→  try {
  88→    await client.query(schemaSql(env.EMBED_DIM))
  89→
  90→    // Fail loudly if the stored vector size no longer matches the configured model
  91→    const { rows } = await client.query<{ dim: number }>(
  92→      `SELECT atttypmod AS dim FROM pg_attribute
  93→       WHERE attrelid = 'document_chunks'::regclass AND attname = 'embedding'`
  94→    )
  95→    if (rows[0] && rows[0].dim !== env.EMBED_DIM) {
  96→      throw new Error(
  97→        `document_chunks.embedding is vector(${rows[0].dim}) but EMBED_DIM=${env.EMBED_DIM}. ` +
  98→          'Re-create the table (or restore the previous EMBED_MODEL) before continuing.'
  99→      )
 100→    }
 101→
 102→    // Jobs that were mid-flight when the server stopped will never finish
 103→    await client.query(
 104→      `UPDATE documents SET status = 'failed', error = 'Interrupted by server restart', updated_at = now()
 105→       WHERE status = 'processing'`
 106→    )
 107→
 108→    ready = true
 109→  } finally {
 110→    client.release()
 111→  }
 112→}
 113→
 114→export async function closeDatabase(): Promise<void> {
 115→  ready = false
 116→  await pool.end()
 117→}
 118→

rawContent.text:
The backend pnpm install is failing because pnpm is trying to delete temporary files (50+ files) in a temporary directory, which triggers the safe-delete guard. The issue is that pnpm uses a content-addressable store and needs to create/manage temporary directories, which involves file operations that the safe-delete shim is blocking.

Let me try a different approach:
1. Use a custom pnpm store directory to avoid the store management issues
2. Or use npm install instead (npm doesn't use a store)

Let me try npm install for the backend. The backend also has a package-lock.json file.

Wait, actually the issue is with the pnpm store. Let me try:
1. Setting a different store-dir
2. Or using npm install with the package-lock.json

Actually, let me try npm install. It should work since the backend has a package-lock.json.

But wait - the backend package.json has `"type": "module"` and the build script uses `tsc` which outputs CommonJS (based on tsconfig.json `"module": "commonjs"`), and then writes `dist/package.json` with `{ type: 'commonjs' }`. The `start` script is `node dist/index.js`.

Actually, looking more carefully at the build script:
```
"build": "tsc && node -e \"require('fs').writeFileSync('dist/package.json', JSON.stringify({ type: 'commonjs' }))\"",
```

This compiles TypeScript with `tsc` (which outputs to `dist/`), then writes a `package.json` file in `dist/` that sets `type: 'commonjs'` so that Node.js treats the .js files as CommonJS modules.

The tsconfig says `"module": "commonjs"` so tsc will output CommonJS modules.

The main package.json has `"type": "module"` but the build creates `dist/package.json` with `type: 'commonjs'` to override this for the dist directory.

So the start command `node dist/index.js` would look for `dist/index.js` (CommonJS) and work.

Let me try using npm to install the backend dependencies. Actually, npm should work fine since it doesn't use a store or symlinks.

  71→  a form anyone can fill) — storage does not require authentication.
  72→- The user wants to **migrate existing local data into the cloud** (browser localStorage, a
  73→  data.json, records.csv, or any local file they have been keeping).
  74→- The user says: 云服务 / 开通云服务 / 后端 / 数据库 / 登录注册 / 文件上传 / AI 能力.
  75→- The user wants to **manage existing resources**: table data, user list, files, model usage.
  76→- The user reports a cloud-service **failure**: data not saved, login broken, upload failing,
  77→  model call erroring.
  78→- The user wants **WeChat mini-program development or publishing**, including changes to an
  79→  existing project, DevTools, real-device debugging, compilation or simulator preview. Load this
  80→  skill for routing even when no backend or publishing capability is requested.
  81→
  82→Do NOT activate a backend for pure static pages, front-end-only interactions with no persistence,
  83→or when the user already picked another backend (their own service, Supabase, …). This does not
  84→exclude the mini-program development routing above.
  85→
  86→## WeChat Mini Program — Route First
  87→
  88→When the request concerns a **WeChat mini program** and asks to create, continue developing,
  89→modify, debug, compile, preview in a simulator, publish, or add a cloud-service capability, read
  90→[`references/mini-program/routing.md`](references/mini-program/routing.md) **before** doing anything
  91→else, and follow the path it directs you to.
  92→
  93→The project type may already be clear from conversation context or a referenced project directory;
  94→the user need not repeat "微信小程序". 「在这个项目上加几个页面」 with an existing WeChat project,
  95→or a follow-up 「我想真机调试看一下效果」, must enter routing before editing code or running
  96→development commands. Neither requires a new cloud-service or publishing intent. Routing alone
  97→does not require calling `workbuddy_cloud_service`.
  98→
  99→Publishing counts on its own, without any backend need. This chain owns mini-program delivery
 100→end to end — code, then upload, audit submission and release from the application space — and it is
 101→also where `appType: "miniprogram"` gets set at app creation. That flag is written **once** and
 102→cannot be corrected later, so a mini program that skips this chain is permanently recorded as a web
 103→app. Never tell the user a mini program cannot be published, or send them to upload it from WeChat
 104→DevTools themselves: managed publishing is available.
 105→
 106→Pure explanations such as 「解释一下小程序的 onLoad 生命周期」 need no routing. Adding or modifying
 107→pages in an existing WeChat project is development work and must enter routing even without a
 108→request to publish.
 109→
 110→Route before acting, not after. The two paths differ in which capabilities they can deliver
 111→(managed publishing and a backend vs. compilation and real-device debugging), and either one becomes
 112→unsafe once you have already started writing files.
 113→
 114→## Activation Confirmation Is UI-Driven — Never Ask It Yourself
 115→
 116→Activation provisions a real resource that may carry quota/billing, so it always needs the user's
 117→go-ahead — **but that go-ahead is collected by the trusted WorkBuddy UI, not by you.** The instant
 118→you determine the app needs a backend, call `action: "activate"` directly; the tool then makes the
 119→WorkBuddy UI pop a confirmation dialog and blocks until the user decides there.
 120→
 121→**NEVER use `AskUserQuestion`, and never ask a natural-language question in chat (e.g. 「要不要开通
 122→云服务？」/「需要我帮你开启后端吗？」), to decide whether to activate.** Doing so bypasses the trusted
 123→confirmation dialog entirely — the UI never pops, and you end up granting or denying a billable
 124→resource on the user's behalf. Making the *decision to call activate* is your job; collecting the
 125→*user's authorization* is the dialog's job. Do not conflate the two.
 126→
 127→- Correct: needs backend → `inspect` → pick the target application (reuse/create) → **call
 128→  `activate` right away** → UI dialog decides whether to enable.
 129→- Wrong: needs backend → ask in chat / via `AskUserQuestion` 「要不要开通」 → (dialog never shown).
 130→  (Asking WHICH application is fine; asking WHETHER to enable is not.)
 131→
 132→The only restraint is: do not activate for something that plainly does not need a backend (see
 133→**When to Use**). If it genuinely needs one, do not pre-ask — activate and let the UI confirm. See
 134→**Confirmation Is Not Yours to Fake** below.
 135→
 136→## Environment Lifecycle
 137→
 138→All four modules share **one** environment. **Never activate per module.**
 139→
 140→### Decision order (mandatory)
 141→
 142→1. Call `workbuddy_cloud_service` with `action: "inspect"` to list the applications registered in
 143→   this session (a session may hold several — see **Which Application** below).
 144→2. Decide which application this request belongs to, then call `action: "activate"` with the right
 145→   `applicationMode`: `"reuse"` + `applicationId` to keep building an existing application, or
 146→   `"create"` + `appName` to start a new independent one. Binding is idempotent and never
 147→   double-charges, so re-activating a reused application to ensure it is on is safe. Do NOT gate the
 148→   activation itself — NEVER use `AskUserQuestion` or a chat question like 「要不要开通」 to decide
 149→   *whether* to enable cloud service; the trusted WorkBuddy UI raises that confirmation dialog and
 150→   the user decides there.
 151→3. Only write cloud-dependent code **after** activation is confirmed successful. Never write code
 152→   against an environment you have not confirmed.
 153→
 154→### Which Application (session may hold several)
 155→
 156→An application comes into being two ways: its cloud service gets activated, or it is published as a
 157→Site. So one conversation can accumulate multiple applications, and you must say which one each
 158→`activate` targets — never let it default to the first.
 159→
 160→- **Reuse an existing application** when the request continues one that already exists: 「继续完善刚才
 161→  的应用」, 「给上面的记账本增加登录」, the user names an existing app, or the need is plainly an
 162→  extension of an existing app's features. Pass `applicationMode: "reuse"` + that `applicationId`
 163→  (from the `inspect` list).
 164→- **Create a new application** when the request starts a separate one: 「再创建一个独立应用」, 「这是另
 165→  一个项目」, 「不要复用刚才的应用」, or the request is for a second project that has not become an
 166→  application yet. Pass `applicationMode: "create"` + a new `appName`.
 167→- **When it is unclear**, you MAY ask the user a plain attribution question — e.g. 「当前会话已有
 168→  『记账本』和『班级相册』，这次需求属于其中一个，还是要新建应用？」 — via ordinary chat or a
 169→  structured question. If you call `activate` without a mode on a non-empty session (or reuse an id
 170→  not in the list, or create a name that already exists), the tool returns a
 171→  `cloud_service_application_selection_required` result with the candidate list and guidance; read
 172→  it, decide, and call again with the right mode.
 173→
 174→⚠️ Asking WHICH application is allowed. Asking WHETHER to enable cloud service is NOT — that stays
 175→with the trusted UI (see the confirmation rules above and in **Confirmation Is Not Yours to Fake**).
 176→
 177→### Publishing After Activation
 178→
 179→Activating is **not** publishing. Activation provisions the backend environment and reserves the
 180→app's share domain; nothing is online until you publish it with the `workbuddy_sites_deploy` tool.
 181→When the user later asks to publish / deploy / 发布 / 上线, **reuse this app's `applicationId` as the
 182→sites tool's `appId`**. Reusing the id keeps the reserved domain (and
 183→therefore the cloud-service Origin); a different domain breaks the app's cloud
 184→login, because the server enforces an exact Origin match. The `applicationId` is the SAME id
 185→used across cloud service and publishing.
 186→
 187→### Status semantics
 188→
 189→On a successful `activate`, `billingStatus` is `normal` (usable) and `provisionStatus` is `assigned`
 190→(bound and ready). Binding is served from a warm pool and returns in seconds — there is **no
 191→"provisioning-in-progress" state to poll**.
 192→
 193→Once the app hits the data plane at runtime, treat runtime errors as the source of truth: quota /
 194→auth / "environment not found" errors mean the user should upgrade or re-enable; do not retry them
 195→as if they were transient.
 196→
 197→### When Binding Can't Succeed Right Now
 198→
 199→Binding is a seconds-level pull from a warm pool — there is no async "provisioning" to poll. When it
 200→cannot succeed, the tool returns a `cloud_service_unavailable` result you must relay:
 201→
 202→- **Pool temporarily empty** — resources are tight. Relay the "try again later" message and stop. The
 203→  user can retry later and you will re-attempt the binding then. Do NOT loop or poll.
 204→- **Account app-quota used up** — the result carries `useLocalImplementation: true`. Relay the message
 205→  AND continue with a local implementation right away (do NOT ask again); a quota banner guides the
 206→  user to upgrade or free an idle app.
 207→- **Backend busy** — relay the "try again later" message and stop.
 208→
 209→## Unpublished Capability & No Silent Downgrade
 210→
 211→If the tool reports the capability is unavailable in this build, or the manager is not wired up,
 212→**say so plainly** and stop. Specifically:
 213→
 214→- **Never invent tool names**, and never poke the cloud-service backend directly through Bash/curl.
 215→- **Never fake success** — don't claim an environment exists, and don't hand back a made-up
 216→  environment id or config.
 217→- **Never silently downgrade** to `localStorage` / an in-memory array / a mock JSON file just to
 218→  make the feature "work". That reads as if the request was fulfilled while the data is not
 219→  actually persisted. If a local-storage-only version is genuinely useful, **ask the user first**
 220→  with a clear yes/no question and only proceed on explicit approval. (This is a **different**
 221→  decision from activation: choosing a local fallback has no trusted UI dialog, so asking here is
 222→  correct — the "never ask, just activate" rule applies only to gating `activate` itself.) The ONE
 223→  exception: when a `cloud_service_unavailable` result carries `useLocalImplementation: true` (e.g.
 224→  the account app-quota is used up), a local fallback is explicitly sanctioned — continue locally
 225→  right away without asking.
 226→- **Never retry to force it through** — not with a different action, not by re-activating.
 227→
 228→## How to Call the Tool
 229→
 230→Use the built-in tool `workbuddy_cloud_service`. It accepts:
 231→
 232→- `action` (required) — `inspect` / `activate`.
 233→- `directory` (required) — absolute path to the app source root. It scopes the session (where the
 234→  local application manifest lives); it does NOT by itself pick WHICH application in the session this
 235→  request targets — express that with `applicationMode` + `applicationId`.
 236→- `applicationMode` (for `activate`) — `"create"` to start a brand-new application (requires
 237→  `appName`; must NOT pass `applicationId`) or `"reuse"` to bind one already registered in this
 238→  session (requires `applicationId`). May be omitted only when the session has no application yet
 239→  (then it is treated as `create`). See **Which Application** above.
 240→- `applicationId` (for `applicationMode: "reuse"` only, required there) — the `wbapp_` id of the
 241→  application to reuse, taken from an `inspect` result's `applications` list.
 242→- `appName` (optional) — a short human-friendly display name **you** summarize from what the app
 243→  actually is (e.g. 「记账本」, 「班级相册」). Keep it under ~10 characters, in the user's language.
 244→  Used when creating a new application; not the directory name, not the conversation title. On
 245→  `reuse` it is ignored (the existing name is kept).
 246→- `intent` (optional, `activate` only) — a short phrase used to build the confirmation dialog title
 247→  **「实现{intent}需要开启云服务」**. Summarize it from the **user's own words** for what they want to
 248→  achieve, and follow these rules:
 249→  - Use the user's **surface wording**, not technical terms: say 「开支记录」 not 「数据」; **never** use
 250→    「数据库」/「身份认证」/「存储」/「云数据库」.
 251→  - If several capabilities are needed, name **at most two**, joined naturally
 252→    (e.g. 「用户登录和积分数据保存」); if **more than two**, pass exactly 「你需要的这些功能」.
 253→  - Keep it in the user's language, ideally ≤ 20 characters.
 254→  - Examples: 「开支记录保存」 → 实现开支记录保存需要开启云服务; 「用户登录」 → 实现用户登录需要开启云服务;
 255→    「用户登录和积分数据保存」 → 实现用户登录和积分数据保存需要开启云服务.
 256→  - This is **display-only**: it does NOT decide whether the dialog pops or whether activation happens
 257→    (that stays with the trusted UI). Omit it and a default title is used — never pass a `confirmed`-like
 258→    value through it.
 259→
 260→A successful call returns JSON with `activated` / `billingStatus` / `provisionStatus` /
 261→`publicConfig` / `message`.
 262→
 263→`publicConfig` carries exactly four fields, and they are the **only** values safe to ship inside
 264→the app's front-end code:
 265→
 266→- `resourceId` — the cloud service resource id.
 267→- `endpoint` — the current application's release-domain data-plane base URL. **Required at client
 268→  initialization — always pass it through** (see **How an App Talks to It**).
 269→- `oauthRelayBaseUrl` — the central OAuth Relay base URL. It backs `signInWithOAuth` in general,
 270→  not one specific provider; **web** WeChat QR sign-in is currently the only provider that uses it.
 271→  Pass it through at initialization in web apps: omitting it makes `signInWithOAuth` fail at
 272→  runtime with `requires oauthRelayBaseUrl`. It is **not** derivable from `endpoint` (that one is
 273→  per-application; the Relay is central). A mini program does not use it.
 274→- `publishableKey` — identifies **which app** and carries **no permissions by itself**; the server
 275→  enforces an exact Origin match. It may live in app source (it ends up visible in the browser
 276→  anyway), but keep it out of logs.
 277→
 278→The underlying environment id and all provider keys stay server-side and are never returned. If a
 279→pattern seems to require the front end to hold a long-lived key, the pattern is wrong.
 280→
 281→### Confirmation Is Not Yours to Fake
 282→
 283→`activate` confirmation is raised by the trusted WorkBuddy UI. The tool
 284→**deliberately rejects** `confirmed` / `confirm` / `skipConfirm` / `force`. Do not attempt to pass
 285→them — passing them means the model is granting itself the user's authorization. **Equally, do NOT
 286→substitute your own question for it: never use `AskUserQuestion` or a chat prompt like 「要不要开通」
 287→to gate activation — that both skips the trusted dialog (it never pops) and quietly self-authorizes.**
 288→If the result carries `declinedByUser: true`, the user said no: that is a **normal outcome, not an
 289→error**. Report it and stop; do not re-ask in a loop or route around it.
 290→
 291→## How an App Talks to It
 292→
 293→The app initializes a client with **both** `endpoint` + `publishableKey` from `publicConfig`, then
 294→calls each module. **Initialize once**; every module reuses that same client instance.
 295→
 296→### `endpoint` is mandatory — never omit it
 297→
 298→Every initialization you generate MUST contain `endpoint: publicConfig.endpoint`. This is not a
 299→style preference:
 300→
 301→Two things are equally forbidden, for the same reason:
 302→
 303→- **Never hard-code an endpoint literal** (`https://xxx.workbuddy.link`, a test/staging domain, …).
 304→  It goes stale the moment the app is republished, and the server's exact-Origin match will reject
 305→  it.
 306→- **Never source it from anywhere but `publicConfig`** — not `window.location`, not an env var, not
 307→  a BFF, not a guessed convention. If you do not have a `publicConfig` in hand, you are not ready to
 308→  write cloud code: go back to **Environment Lifecycle** and activate first.
 309→
 310→Data-plane paths are fixed (all under `/.cloud/` so they cannot collide with the app's own routes):
 311→
 312→| Module | Path |
 313→|---|---|
 314→| Auth | `/.cloud/auth/v1/**`, `/.cloud/auth/v2/**` |
 315→| Database | `/.cloud/database/rest/**` |
 316→| Storage | `/.cloud/storage/**` |
 317→| LLM API | `/.cloud/llm/chat/completions` |
 318→
 319→The client is `@tencent-ai/workbuddy-cloud-sdk`, shipped in **three** forms: the npm root entry, the
 320→CDN `<script>` global, and the npm `/miniprogram` subpath. Pick by the project shape — the module
 321→APIs are **identical** in all three, so module docs are written once and apply to every form. Do not
 322→initialize a second CloudBase client or hand-write module fetch wrappers.
 323→
 324→### Which form to use
 325→
 326→| Project shape | Form |
 327→|---|---|
 328→| Has `package.json` + bundler (Vite / Next / Webpack / RN …) | **npm package** — falls back to CDN if the install fails |
 329→| WeChat native miniprogram (has a build step: 「构建 npm」) | **npm package, `/miniprogram` subpath** — see Form A's 小程序 branch |
 330→| Single-file HTML, no build step, no npm (HTML artifacts, small games, one-page demos) | **CDN `<script>`** |
 331→
 332→Never mix forms in one project, and never introduce a package manager or bundler into a
 333→plain-HTML project just to install the SDK. The **only** legitimate reason to leave the form the
 334→table picked is a failed npm install (see Form A below) — and that **switches** a web project to the
 335→CDN form, it never leaves the project on both. A miniprogram has no CDN form to switch to: fix the
 336→install instead.
 337→
 338→### Form A — npm package (projects with a build step)
 339→
 340→Install from the `dev` channel. Do not pin a specific version and do not invent a version number —
 341→during integration the SDK ships fixes on the `dev` tag, and a pinned version silently freezes the
 342→app on older behaviour (`latest` is **not** maintained yet, so it also points at a stale build):
 343→
 344→```bash
 345→npm install @tencent-ai/workbuddy-cloud-sdk@dev
 346→# pnpm add / yarn add — same specifier
 347→```
 348→
 349→```ts
 350→import { createWorkBuddyCloud } from '@tencent-ai/workbuddy-cloud-sdk'
 351→
 352→export const cloud = createWorkBuddyCloud({
 353→  endpoint: publicConfig.endpoint,
 354→  oauthRelayBaseUrl: publicConfig.oauthRelayBaseUrl,
 355→  publishableKey: publicConfig.publishableKey,
 356→})
 357→```
 358→
 359→Ships ESM (`import`), CJS (`require`) and bundled `.d.ts`, so TypeScript needs no extra setup.
 360→
 361→#### If the install fails, fall back to the CDN
 362→
 363→A build-based project still **starts** with npm. But the install can fail for reasons you cannot fix
 364→from inside the project — no registry access, the pinned dev version not reachable from this
 365→network, auth errors on the `@tencent-ai` scope, or a sandbox with no network at all. When that
 366→happens, **do not** stall, do not ask the user to fix their registry, and above all **do not
 367→hand-write fetch wrappers or pull in a second CloudBase client** — switch this project to the
 368→CDN form (Form B) instead:
 369→
 370→1. Load the IIFE build from the CDN and use the `WorkBuddyCloud` global, exactly as Form B
 371→   describes. In a bundler project, the `<script>` goes in the HTML entry (e.g. `index.html`), not
 372→   in a module `import`.
 373→2. Remove the failed dependency from `package.json` so the project does not carry a phantom
 374→   dependency that breaks the next `install` / CI run.
 375→3. Tell the user, in one line, that the SDK is loaded from the CDN because the npm install failed —
 376→   it changes how the app is served (needs network at runtime, no bundled types), so it must not be
 377→   silent.
 378→
 379→Retry the `@dev` npm specifier **once** before switching; if it fails again, switch and move on
 380→rather than looping. Everything after initialization is unchanged, so no module code needs rewriting
 381→— only the import/init site differs.
 382→
 383→#### 小程序（微信原生，有构建步骤）
 384→
 385→A WeChat native miniprogram has a build step (「构建 npm」 in the devtools) but **no browser
 386→runtime**: no global `fetch`, no `localStorage`, no `location.origin`. It uses the npm form
 387→through the dedicated subpath `@tencent-ai/workbuddy-cloud-sdk/miniprogram`, and only the
 388→factory that subpath exports:
 389→
 390→Before initializing, follow [Mini-Program Cloud Request Diagnostics](references/mini-program/diagnostics.md)
 391→to copy the bundled helper into the mini-program project. Import it relative to the initialization
 392→file (`./workbuddy-cloud-diagnostics` below assumes `utils/cloud.js`), then wrap only this client's
 393→`wx` instance. Existing projects keep their installed SDK version; diagnostics needs no SDK upgrade.
 394→
 395→```js
 396→const { createMiniProgramWorkBuddyCloud } = require('@tencent-ai/workbuddy-cloud-sdk/miniprogram')
 397→const { createDiagnosticWx } = require('./workbuddy-cloud-diagnostics')
 398→
 399→const cloud = createMiniProgramWorkBuddyCloud({
 400→  endpoint: publicConfig.endpoint,
 401→  publishableKey: publicConfig.publishableKey,
 402→  wx: createDiagnosticWx(wx),
 403→})
 404→
 405→module.exports = { cloud }
 406→```
 407→
 408→- Still pass **both** `publicConfig` values. A miniprogram has no `location.origin`, so the
 409→  SDK's same-origin fallback does not exist here — omitting `endpoint` fails at initialization.
 410→- The factory returns the same client shape as Form A (`cloud.auth` / `cloud.database` /
 411→  `cloud.storage` / `cloud.llm`); the module docs below apply unchanged. Internally it wires the
 412→  miniprogram polyfills, the `wx.request`-backed fetch and the `wx` storage in one fixed order —
 413→  that ordering is the SDK's job now, not the app's.
 414→- Do **not** import `createWorkBuddyCloud` from the root entry and hand-assemble
 415→  `createMiniProgramFetch` / `createMiniProgramStorage` / `ensureMiniProgramPolyfills` yourself:
 416→  skipping or reordering any step yields a client that constructs fine and fails on the first
 417→  request. Do **not** call `wx.request` directly against the data plane either — that bypasses
 418→  publishableKey injection and session management.
 419→- The CDN `<script>` form (Form B) does not **apply** to miniprograms — there is no HTML entry to
 420→  host the IIFE global, so it is the wrong shape rather than a missing capability. The
 421→  install-failure fallback above therefore does not switch forms here: fix the npm install instead
 422→  (network / registry). Never replace SDK module calls with hand-written `wx.request`, and never tell the
 423→  user the SDK does not support miniprograms — the `/miniprogram` subpath is the supported form.
 424→
 425→### Form B — CDN `<script>` (plain HTML, no build step)
 426→
 427→```html
 428→<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tencent-ai/workbuddy-cloud-sdk@dev/lib/index.global.js"></script>
 429→<script>
 430→  const cloud = WorkBuddyCloud.createWorkBuddyCloud({
 431→    endpoint: publicConfig.endpoint,
 432→    oauthRelayBaseUrl: publicConfig.oauthRelayBaseUrl,
 433→    publishableKey: publicConfig.publishableKey,
 434→  })
 435→</script>
 436→```
 437→
 438→- The IIFE build exposes the global `WorkBuddyCloud`; every export is reached through it
 439→  (`WorkBuddyCloud.createWorkBuddyCloud`, `WorkBuddyCloud.CLOUD_MODULE_PATHS`, …). There is **no**
 440→  bare global `createWorkBuddyCloud`.
 441→- Initialize **after** the script has loaded — no synchronous calls from `<head>`, and no
 442→  `type="module"` / `import` against the CDN URL.
 443→- Use the `@dev` channel, **not** `@latest`: `latest` is not maintained yet and points at a stale
 444→  build. Do not substitute a pinned version either — during integration the fixes land on `dev`.
 445→
 446→Everything after initialization is the same object shape in all three forms — read the module docs
 447→below for concrete API signatures, and translate `import { X }` to `WorkBuddyCloud.X` when on the CDN
 448→path. **Do not re-read module docs per form.**
 449→
 450→## Module Docs
 451→
 452→**Read only the files the current request touches — never load all modules up front.** Decide
 453→which modules the request hits, then read from the table below; one task usually needs 1–2 files.
 454→
 455→`code-generation` is for **writing app code**; `management` is for **inspecting and maintaining
 456→existing resources**. Different purposes — do not mix them up.
 457→
 458→Auth and Storage `management.md` also define how the WorkBuddy management UI should interpret
 459→Provider/capability state and business errors. They are not model-callable tools: use them for
 460→troubleshooting and implementation guidance, and do not invent a service-role credential or direct
 461→provider fallback.
 462→
 463→### Database
 464→
 465→- Write app code: `references/database/code-generation.md`
 466→- Inspect and manage data: `references/database/management.md`
 467→
 468→### Auth
 469→
 470→- Write auth code: `references/auth/code-generation.md`
 471→- Manage auth config and users: `references/auth/management.md`
 472→
 473→### Storage
 474→
 475→- Write file storage code: `references/storage/code-generation.md`
 476→- Manage files and directories: `references/storage/management.md`
 477→
 478→### LLM API
 479→
 480→- Write LLM call code: `references/llm/code-generation.md`
 481→- Inspect models and usage: `references/llm/management.md`
 482→
 483→## Important Rules
 484→
 485→- **Secrets never land in code.** No long-lived keys or admin credentials in front-end code, repo
 486→  files or logs. The front end uses only end-user-facing public config.
 487→- **The client is always initialized from `publicConfig`.** `endpoint` and `publishableKey` are
 488→  mandatory at every `createWorkBuddyCloud` call site, and a **web** app also passes
 489→  `oauthRelayBaseUrl` (needed for WeChat QR sign-in). Never rely on the SDK's optional-`endpoint`
 490→  same-origin fallback, never hard-code an endpoint literal, and never read it from `location` /
 491→  env vars / a BFF (see **How an App Talks to It**).
 492→- **Never print sensitive values.** End-user tokens, phone numbers, emails and private file URLs
 493→  stay out of logs and out of your reply.
 494→- **Isolate data per user.** Any read/write of user data must carry an identity constraint; no user
 495→  may read or write another user's data.
 496→- **Destructive operations need explicit confirmation.** Dropping tables, clearing data or
 497→  bulk-deleting files — state the blast radius and irreversibility first.
 498→- **Stay in scope.** Only touch the current app's environment; never read or write another app's
 499→  resources.
 500→- **Validate uploads.** Constrain type and size; never trust the client-supplied filename or path.
 501→- Do not surface internal details (raw backend endpoints, internal ids beyond what
 502→  `publicConfig` exposes) to the user.
 503→
 504→## Delivering artifacts
 505→
 506→An application delivery must produce **exactly one application card** — web app or WeChat mini
 507→program alike. So `present_files` is called with **only** the `.genie` marker
 508→(`.<applicationId>.genie`, returned as `genieFilePath` when the application is created) — pass the
 509→path as-is.
 510→
 511→- **Never omit the marker.** It is what registers the application; without it there is no card.
 512→- **Never pass anything else in that call.** Not the entry HTML, not `project.config.json` or
 513→  `app.json`, not pages, components, source files, `sitemap.json` or `README`, and never the
 514→  mini-program privacy manifest. Every extra path becomes its own artifact card beside the
 515→  application, turning a clean delivery into a pile of files the user cannot act on.
 516→
 517→Because no page is delivered as an artifact, the marker is the only thing that can point at the
 518→app's local entry. **For a web app, write `entryHtml` into the `.genie` file** — a relative path
 519→inside the app directory with a `.html` / `.htm` suffix (`entryHtml: index.html`,
 520→`entryHtml: pages/home.html`); never absolute, never `..`, never a URL. Leave every other field
 521→untouched. A mini program has no entry HTML, so leave `entryHtml` unset there.
 522→
 523→**Never mention the `.genie` file, its path, or this call in your reply.** It is internal artifact
 524→tracking; describing it hands the user a hidden YAML file they have no use for. Refer to what they
 525→see: the application card.
 526→
 527→## Completion Bar
 528→
 529→A cloud-service task is done only when **all** of these hold:
 530→
 531→1. Environment confirmed usable — `billingStatus` is `normal` or `expiring`, and `provisionStatus`
 532→   is `assigned`.
 533→2. Every module the request needs is integrated per its `code-generation.md`, and the code runs.
 534→   Every client call site in the generated source passes `endpoint` and `publishableKey` — plus
 535→   `oauthRelayBaseUrl` in a web app that offers WeChat sign-in — all sourced from `publicConfig`.
 536→   Grep for `createWorkBuddyCloud` **and** `createMiniProgramWorkBuddyCloud` and check each hit
 537→   before reporting done.
 538→3. The critical path is actually verified: written data reads back; login yields an identity;
 539→   an uploaded file can be downloaded or opened through its signed URL; the model call returns.
 540→4. Failure paths are handled: network failure, not-logged-in, insufficient permission and
 541→   out-of-quota all produce a clear message — nothing fails silently.
 542→5. Your report to the user states what was activated, which modules were integrated, and how to
 543→   verify it — plus any quota or billing implications.
 544→6. **WeChat mini programs only** — the privacy manifest `.<applicationId>.privacy.json` (a hidden
 545→   file, leading dot included, e.g. `.wbapp_a1b2c3.privacy.json`) **MUST** be written at the
 546→   project root, enumerating every privacy capability the generated code exercises. See C5 in
 547→   [`references/mini-program/routing.md`](references/mini-program/routing.md); the key list,
 548→   derivation rules and the reporting rules (write it silently) are in
 549→   [`references/mini-program/privacy-manifest.md`](references/mini-program/privacy-manifest.md).
 550→7. **Artifacts are delivered narrowly** — one `present_files` call carrying only the `.genie`
 551→   marker, nothing else. See [Delivering artifacts](#delivering-artifacts).
 552→
 553→For a WeChat mini program, items 3 and 4 are relaxed exactly as
 554→[`references/mini-program/routing.md`](references/mini-program/routing.md) C4 describes, because
 555→nothing is compiled or run on that path. That relaxation covers **verification only** — it is not a
 556→licence to report the delivery as unshippable, nor an invitation to itemize what you could not verify:
 557→C4 says to report the outcome rather than the procedure. Publishing is available, and the report
 558→**must end** with the 「如何预览和发布」 block that C3 specifies.
